summary: Read-only content-completion/page/media routes acquire User/Session/Creation row locks across a native subprocess, blocking administrative revocation that their final fresh authorization is intended to observe.
evidence: Existing PostgreSQL final-after-real-Node membership revoke test hung after three cases passed. Dedicated-QA pg_stat_activity confirmed admin UPDATE control_memberships transactionid wait blocked by the request's idle transaction; metadata retained before cancelling only that exact owned QA query.
All three read-only content_completion/routes.py endpoints call owned(lock=True), whose canonical reader locks User, Session and Creation before waiting for the native transport.
rollback: Revert only these read-only route lock selections and their focused regression/doc changes. Preserve first blocked/cancelled test and bounded lock failures. No operating database restore, authority/final-fence removal, change to mutation locking, RLS or heartbeat limits.
